Docs/Policy integration

Policy integration

Build an adapter that preserves the environment's observation, action and stage-transition contract.

Define the adapter boundary

Your policy adapter translates the environment observation into model inputs and model predictions into controller targets. It should preserve the task's reset, success, termination and truncation behavior. Begin with one canonical stage and a short recorded rollout before attempting a full evaluation matrix.

  1. Read the registered robot, controller, action space and camera profile.
  2. Map images, proprioception, history and language into the model schema.
  3. Undo action normalization and convert predicted coordinates into the environment's joint order.
  4. Execute the chosen number of chunk actions at the 20 Hz control rate.
  5. At episode reset, clear policy history and cached action chunks.

Convert coordinates explicitly

Sharpa single-arm control has 29 absolute joint targets; bimanual control has 58. The bimanual order is left arm, right arm, left hand, right hand. These layouts describe Sharpa and do not specify the spaces of every supported embodiment.

The GR00T reference adapter uses relative arm offsets internally and converts them back to absolute pd_joint_pos targets. Finger targets remain absolute. Passing offsets directly to the controller produces a different action even when the array has the expected width.

Adapter componentCheck before evaluation
ImagesDataset camera → environment sensor mapping, color channels, resize/crop, normalization and history.
StateField selection/order, task-dependent width, units and training-time statistics.
ActionsJoint order, radians, absolute/relative conversion, clipping and inverse normalization.
ChunksPrediction horizon, executed actions per query and behavior when an episode ends mid-chunk.
LanguageCanonical or registered instruction selection and any stage-specific instruction update.

Compose stages without resetting the scene

For a complete sequence, reset once at the beginning. Use the task's stage-success signals to update the instruction or select the next stage policy while preserving the simulator state. Resetting objects between stages changes the long-horizon task into separate skill evaluations.

The paper's π0.5 composition switches stage-specific policies when a stage succeeds. GR00T uses a pooled task model with stage instructions. If your model keeps observation history or an action queue, define how those are handled when the stage changes and record that rule with the experiment.

Use the reference path and record your changes

Research checkout required

The module examples on this page require an asset-complete research checkout, its compatible Python environment, and the relevant simulator or model dependencies. The current public repository ↗ contains a README, license and repository metadata; cloning it does not provide the task modules, robot assets, datasets or checkpoints used below. These examples document the verified research interfaces.

Inspect algo/groot.py, train/train_groot.py and train/train_configs/groot_config.py for the in-process GR00T path. ACT and Diffusion Policy expose their own image/state adapters and camera mappings in their training configurations.

Keep the environment constructor separate from the model adapter so make_scene_eval_env can supply the fixed native-scene environment without changing the policy. Save the adapter revision, checkpoint hash, input schema and preprocessing configuration. Use Quick evaluation to validate the loop, then Scene evaluation to test transfer.
